segments.text: A Quantum-Driven Trust-Aware Optimization Framework for Secure and Energy-Efficient Healthcare IoT Networks Abstract-The explosive growth of IoT devices in the healthcare system increases the pressure over the issues of data security, trust management and energy utilization. Typical cryptographic and clustering approaches fall short as they are unable to effectively tackle dynamic threats like DDoS attacks and node-level compromises. In this study, a QIoT framework is proposed for the improved security, trust and energy-saving healthcare data communication in WSNs. The resultant model Fuses Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), Trust aware Mountain Gazelle Optimization (TMGO) and dynamic trust based on residual energy for intelligent CH selection in WSN. The system further includes a quantum-inspired anomalous detection function acting to detect and mitigate DDoS attacks in real-time, thereby enabling secure uninterrupted communication of data throughout the network. Simulations conducted in MATLAB for WSN with 100-nodes show the better performance of our proposed (QIoT-TMGO) as compared to benchmark approaches: LEACHTM, DGTTSSA and eeTMFOGA. The model increases network stability by 24%, raises the average trust up to 32% and maintains over 95% data delivery rate under 10% malicious nodes. It also significantly improves energy-efficiency metrics including FND, HND and LND, which indicates that it is robust and suitable for secure and sustainable healthcare systems. Keywords- Quantum IoT, Wireless Sensor Networks, Healthcare Data Security, Quantum Key Distribution, Trust-aware Clustering, Meta-Heuristic Optimization, DDoS Mitigation, Energy Efficiency. I Introduction The incorporation of Internet of Things technologies within healthcare infrastructure has provided aid in real-time patient monitoring, decision-making data in treatment, and the management of chronic conditions. The remote sensing devices, wearable monitor & ambient diagnostic platforms are the integrated wireless ecosystem that monitors and transmits health-related data necessary for accurate prediction decisions about patients. However, this network expansion poses some challenges, especially in data privacy issues, node reliability, and energy efficiency [1],[2],[3]. Nevertheless, existing frameworks based on either traditional cryptographic models or lightweight routing protocols are more or less ill-suited to be prepared against adversarial behaviors or coordinated attacks [4],[5]. Furthermore, healthcare IoT deployments usually (most if not all of the time) concern highly resource-constrained environments where conventional security overheads cannot be supported [6], [7]. Dimensioning cluster mechanisms disregard node trustworthiness [8], [9], leading to windows of opportunity for inside compromises, and reactive security systems are too late for life-critical medical applications [10],[11]. In situations such as remote care or emergency services, trust-based communication and secure data aggregation are indispensable. However, many existing models only study the latter type of behaviors in which seemingly cooperative nodes can disrupt CH elections and change data flows [12],[13]. Although a variety of protocols serve for energy- aware routing or secure key exchange alone, few can combine these issues in one responsive architecture [14], [15], [16]. In healthcare scenarios, we believe that applications are prone to highly spread (e.g., vírus)-distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks which can be generated from infected but apparently operational nodes, making reactive anomaly detection ineffective [17], [18]. Trust metrics employed in the decision making of routing rely on fixed thresholds or lagged behaviour analysis which all makes it incapable of finding

Without DQKA, the real-time QRSAsU8 security mechanism of healthcare networks is lacking and subject to spoofing/replay attacks as in particular those taking place at CH level with data fusion [20], [21]. The Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) is based on the no-cloning theorem and quantum entanglement, which can be secure against a quantum-capable adversary who can do nothing for it [14], such that we know how to prove [21]. On the other hand integrating QKD in WSN was not attempted much because of its problem overhead, scalability and integration complexity [22], [23]. The QKD is combined with a trust-aware clustering mechanism, managed by an on-demand meta-heuristic optimization technique that enables making such decision adaptive and responsive to balance between trust decaying r and the remaining energy at node n [24], [25] thus ensuring secure routing activities in real-time while under adversarial environments, without trading off the life of the system or reducing its scalability. It is obvious that this potential can only be realized if combined with a comprehensive architecture in which secure KE, adaptive trust modeling, and energy-efficient CH selection are effectively integrated. Unlike typical static security policies that assume nodes are stable over time, frequent reevaluation of trust is needed in healthcare environments because usage patterns change over time; the quantity of health data changes; and the extent of anomalies at node level increases. In reality, the employed attack is to exploit remaining energy metrics by adversaries and attempt to fulfill CH that can be eliminated in case a recent mechanism (behavioral trust analytics) is incorporated into the optimization model [3], [9], [13]. In this paper, we introduce the Trust-aware Mountain Gazelle Optimization (TMGO) algorithm and apply it for multi-objectives CH selection using trust scores obtained from direct and indirect monitoring results along with energy levels as well as QKD handshake success rates. To enrich the DF-CUDA system, we introduce a new quantum-inspired anomaly detection mechanism that focuses on describing DDoS signatures when the quantum key lifetime is updated and when a message travels indefinitely before it is received. In tandem, this will allow the network to natively preempt rogue nodes, reroute sensitive data, and save energy. The impact of end-to-end analysis results: Our proposed QIoT system provides greater network security, trusted estimation and data communication efficiency in hostile environments, which is verified by the experiment conducted by us in healthcare examples [7], [15], [17], [21]. The paper makes three main contributions: ●​ Towards a hybrid QIoT architecture by using Quantum Key Distribution and trust aware cluster head selection for enhanced data confidentiality, integrity, and energy efficiency in health care sensor networks. ●​ The Quantum -inspired Anomaly Based DDoS detection mechanism that can be used for a real-time proactive detection and mitigation of the DDoS attack and is specifically designed to support the resource constrained medical devices. ●​ Development of dynamic and secure cluster formation algorithm with trust metrics based on multi-parametric inputs such as energy levels, etc., termed as Trust-aware Mountain Gazelle Optimization (TMGO). ●​ Extensive simulation and MATLAB-based evaluation demonstrate that the proposed scheme significantly outperforms LEACH-TM, DGTTSSA, and eeTMFOGA on trust accuracy, delivery reliability and energy consumption metrics. The remainder of the paper is structured as follows. The related works section reviews prior efforts in trust-based clustering and secure healthcare IoT. The methodology outlines the proposed QIoT-TMGO framework and its core components. Experimental results and comparisons are presented, followed by the conclusion and future directions.

The proposed QIoT-TMGO framework distinctly outperforms by offering a holistic, quantum-secured, and trust-optimized solution. 2.1 Research Gap​ Despite the developments in secure IoT-empowered healthcare platforms, today's models still do not inherently accommodate the dynamic adaptability to resource constraints at runtime encryption. Existing trust-aware clustering methods usually do not consider energy consumption as well as uncertainty of behaviors in the harsh environment. There are few practical wireless sensor network architectures that include quantum level security features such as QKD. Most of the energy efficient routing approaches do not consider malicious node detection at time of data aggregation. The machine learning-based and reinforcement methods enhance routing, but not much resilient to DDoS-like traffic pattern. Most existing solutions also consider security, trust, and energy management separately. However, an involved quantum-secure trust-based optimization framework is still significantly unexplored for healthcare IoT networks. III Proposed Work​ The proposed work introduces a quantum trust system along with an energy-efficient secure architecture for healthcare devices in IoT. Integral to this architecture is the incorporation of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), whereby secure cryptographic keys are generated using quantum mechanics, making them invulnerable against eavesdropping or key compromise even against a quantum computer. This paper introduces a Trust-aware Mountain Gazelle Optimization (TMGO) algorithm to find the optimal cluster head that balances between energy management and trust at the same time in light of residual energy, communication reliability, and past behavior. In contrast to a static clustering, this mechanism is able to adjust according to network dynamics and malicious behaviors. Inspired by existing initiatives that have previously prioritized privacy-preserving lightweight designs in medical IoT [33], the framework improves data routing by focusing on nodes that have high trust scores while at the same time depleting less energy. The clustering phase also reduces communication overhead, leading to a longer sustainable IoMT routing lifetime [26],[27]. Additionally, a lightweight anomaly

The layer operates in the background, does not interfere with core communication, and helps maintain throughput and stability in real time. It adapts the learning on-the-fly based on network behavior, which is similar to findings in energy-efficient data inference frameworks [32] by ensuring security and performance. In conclusion, the approach provides a dependable, scalable method suited to data-heavy healthcare applications of a sensitive nature. [30],[31]. In this work, we employ the BB84 protocol for secure key reconciliation among cluster heads and base stations. BB84 transmits quantum (qubits) states in one of the rectilinear or diagonal bases; this choice is made at random. All qubits measured in the same basis are used for storing the final secret key. segments.text: 3.3 Trust-aware Mountain Gazelle Optimization (TMGO) Algorithm​ In this work, the TMGO algorithm as a fundamental metaheuristic is selected, based on its biological background that simulates the behavior of gazelles under threatening environments; such maneuver concept in nature is essential with regard to dynamic and energy labour routing problem (D&ELRP) for healthcare WSNs. In contrast to static optimization approaches, TMGO is light weight and adapted, which suits the constrained environment, such as IoT-based medical applications [26]. The decentralized nature of our proposed scheme matches well with clustered network topologies that allow individual sensor nodes to independently check local trust and energy status before selecting an optimal CH. Expanding the classical MGO with trust-awareness, the model appropriately provides solutions to essential weaknesses in the current clustering technologies, using either only based on energy metrics or by depending on historical node performance. Figure 2: Trust-aware Mountain Gazelle Optimization (TMGO) Framework for Cluster Head Selection in IoT-enabled Healthcare WSNs The application of the TMGO algorithm in an IoT-based healthcare WSN model is presented in Figure 2. Every sensor node assess its own trust level and remaining energy locally before feeding into the TMGO based optimization, which replicates gazelle group behavior when in danger. Using trust and energy criteria, best cluster heads (CHs) are chosen to collect information at the BS effectively. This self-organizing and adaptive model can improve the security and energy saving of medical IoTs.

In the optimization procedure, search agents’ positions are updated iteratively by using the TMGO algorithm and its time complexity is O(I × n × d), where I = number of iterations, d = dimension of solution space. Recalibration of trust scores and anomaly detection modules have per round time complexity that is read once, with extra O(n) contribution. The total complexity for a full cycle of data routing and trust-aware optimization is O(n + I n d), which makes it possible to implement in practice for large-scale healthcare IoT networks. This lean design ultimately enables the model to work towards the real-time, energy aware secured communication without bogging down edge or base-station resources.

IV Implementation Details​ Through a simulation-driven approach, a proposed QIoT framework was evaluated against trust-aware routing, energy efficiency, and adversarial scenarios. The healthcare network topology was modeled as dense, with static patient nodes (which means that the patients are not allowed to move), dynamic wireless mobile sensors, and base stations that were deployed in the monitored zones. Simulations were conducted to compute the First Node Death (FND), Last Node Death (LND), average trust index, delivery ratio, throughput, and packet loss in both normal and attack-injected scenarios. To explore the sensitivity of our model to detect attacks and how efficiently it can provide mitigation, we systematically initiate various attacks, including selective forwarding, DDoS floods, and misrouting behavior. Performance was tested against three traditional trust-based and energy-aware routing protocols in comparative benchmarking to determine increases in node longevity and communication legitimacy. In particular, we evaluated the impact of the TMGO algorithm on stabilization and global data delivery delay in terms of CHs over four metrics: route rediscovery time and packet overhead (both of which are lower), as well as the number of CH updates at each round (the former measure was higher). QKD integration took this further, enabling the link security to be increased without sacrificing network responsiveness. On the whole, simulations found that the model was capable of preserving reliable trust-centric communication while fairly compensating energy and privacy-preserving constraints with respect to routing decisions under fluctuating healthcare traffic conditions. 4.1 Experimentation Setup​ The simulations were implemented in MATLAB R2023b by running a 64-bit Windows 11 on the machine, Intel Core i7-12700 processor, equipped with 16 GB DDR4 RAM and SSD for fast data processing. The simulation space is a 100m × 100m grid with sensor nodes distributed randomly and has been set up to include 200 sensor nodes, each of which starts with maximum energy given by 2J. The radio energy model used the first-order of communication costs all over the world: and . The packet size was set at 512 bytes and simulations 𝐸𝑡𝑥= 50𝑛𝐽/𝑏𝑖𝑡 𝐸𝑎𝑚𝑝= 100𝑝𝐽/𝑏𝑖𝑡/𝑚 2 performed for 2000 rounds to ensure that the results corresponded to the long term network behavior. QKD sessions were modeled based on a probabilistic key-sharing layer, connected with MATLAB Simulink for custom modeling of quantum characteristics. For each round dynamic trust values were computed on the basis of real-time packet delivery ratio, remaining energy, and interaction logs. We designed a custom MATLAB function for the metaheuristic module, the TMGO which deals with processing of fitness values iteratively during cluster head selection. The model's 24% ability to prolong network stability is an avenue to the way in which these TMGO-driven clusters help with intelligent energy distribution and load balancing among sensor nodes. This is due to its trust-aware architecture that modifies node behavior sprouting from its deviations, ultimately mitigating the influence of any compromised nodes as evidenced by a significant 32% improvement in average trust score. Even with 10% of the nodes behaving maliciously, the system maintains a higher than 95% data delivery ratio, which none of the eight state-of-the-art models can achieve. In other words, the framework enables secure and effective data routing due to its solution in quantum key distribution (made for encryption) combined with decentralized trust computation that helps in deriving the maximum benefit of them all. Furthermore, in FND, HND, and LND challenges, the nodes die relatively late, where each challenge was delayed, which provides additional evidence for its extended degree of network resilience under adversarial conditions to be operated for real-time critical healthcare monitoring applications. VI Conclusion​ In this study, we have developed a secure and energy-efficient QIoT-TMGO mechanism for the IoMT system through combining Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), trust-aware analytics, and MGO for dynamic clustering. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that the proposed model significantly outperforms eight state-of-the-art protocols in terms of key metrics. It particularly increases the network stability up to 24%, trust average scores up by 32% and obtains a data delivery ratio of 95.6% even with the presence of 10% malicious nodes infected into it. Moreover, the model further reaches First Node Death (FND) at 350 rounds, Half Node Death (HND) at 700 and Last Node Death (LND) at 1100 which demonstrates significant energy resilience. These findings show the framework to be reliable, robust and applicable for real-time communication of healthcare data even under adversarial circumstances. As future work, we will extend the model to mobility-aware scenarios and integrate blockchain-based audit trails for trust transparency.We also plan to validate performance on real hardware testbeds in clinical deployments.
